step1.title: What kind of correction is this?
step1.lede: You never type the mistakes in as a list. You write the sentence the way the student meets it, and the sentence the way it should be — the builder works out what separates them, and that becomes the mistakes to find.

modeHelp.sentences: One mistake per sentence is the norm.
modeHelp.passage: Three to five mistakes in one paragraph.

step1.sentencesNote: Each sentence stands on its own. Students can correct them in any order.
step1.passageNote: The whole paragraph is one submission. Students are not told which sentence holds the mistake.

step1.textHelp: Shown beside the table on a wide screen, above it on a phone.
step1.presetRgsDesc: Adds the honest third answer, for claims the text says nothing about.
step1.presetSuDesc: When «riktig» would read as «correct» rather than «true».
step1.presetNote: A preset rebuilds the columns and keeps the answers whose name survives.
step1.shortHelp: The short code is what a bulk paste and the CSV export use.
step1.removeColumnFloor: A table keeps at least two columns.
step1.addColumnCeiling: Four columns is the most a table can have.

step2.title: The statements
step2.lede: One row per claim about the text. Mark the right column as you write — the shared key is what makes the whole table checkable in one go.
step2.readyHelp: A statement is ready when it has text and a marked answer.
step2.statementPlaceholder: Syklister må ha lys foran og bak i mørket.
step2.removeFloor: The table keeps at least one row.
step2.bulkHelp: One statement per line. Put the answer after a | using the short code, the full name or the column number. Lines without a marker arrive unanswered.
step2.bulkPlaceholder:
Syklister må ha lys foran og bak. | R
Reglene gjelder bare om vinteren. | G
step2.bulkNote: The empty rows already in the table are replaced by what you paste. Everything written stays.
step2.bulkParsed: {count, plural, one {# statement} other {# statements}}, {marked} with an answer.

step3.title: How much help
step3.lede: The table is checked as one submission. These settings decide what happens after that first check.
step3.retryHelp: A retry reopens only the statements they got wrong.
step3.lockCorrectLabel: Lock the rows they got right
step3.lockCorrectHelp: Correct answers freeze; a retry only reopens the wrong ones.
step3.revealKeyLabel: Reveal the key when the checks run out
step3.revealKeyHelp: The right column is marked on every row they missed.
step3.shuffleRowsHelp: A different order per attempt. The columns never move.
step3.numberingHelp: 1. 2. 3. in front of each row — worth keeping if you refer to them in class.
step3.showTextLabel: Show the text with the table
step3.showTextHelp: Beside the table on a wide screen, above it on a phone. Off means they answer from memory.
step3.progressHelp: A progress strip above the table while they work.

step4.title: Why each answer is what it is
step4.lede: This is where the table stops being a quiz. One line per statement, pointing at the place in the text that settles it.
step4.coverageQuoted: {count, plural, =0 {No statement quotes a line from the text.} one {# statement quotes a line from the text.} other {# statements quote a line from the text.}}
step4.whyHelp: Shown under the statement once the table is checked.
step4.whyPlaceholder: Point at the text, not at the rule.
step4.whyPlaceholderKey: Why this is «{label}» — point at the text, not at the rule.
step4.quoteHelp: Shown with the explanation, in the words of the text.
step4.quotePlaceholder: må alle som sykler i mørket ha lys både foran og bak
step4.empty: Statements with text and a marked answer show up here for their explanation.
